claims.claim: Mean disruption percentile decreases and median citations increase with team size, including the extension to 100 authors.
claims.evidence_needed: Design-weighted within-year ranks, stratum means and medians, uncertainty and counts.
claims.reason: Recent single-institution OpenAlex works, not the historical multi-population corpus.

claims.claim: The disruption distribution differs by team size, beyond mean differences.
claims.evidence_needed: Distribution plots and contrasts with t and KS tests or design-aware analogues.
claims.reason: Testable within the Columbia sampling frame where both counts and D are available.

claims.claim: The disruption gradient holds across impact levels and is strongest at high impact.
claims.evidence_needed: Weighted within-year citation rank groups; stratum curves, slope/interaction, counts and intervals.
claims.reason: Unequal/short follow-up and sample precision limit impact comparisons.

claims.claim: The disruption gradient holds across fields and subfields and within most journals.
claims.evidence_needed: OpenAlex primary topic hierarchy and venue gradients with uncertainty, group sizes and ascertainment rules.
claims.reason: Alternate classifications, one institutional cohort and limited journal/group coverage.

claims.claim: Larger teams cite newer and more highly cited references; age and popularity distribution parameters vary with team size.
claims.evidence_needed: Deduplicated focal-reference pairs with year/current citation totals; compare distributions, assess exponential and power-law fits and quantify coverage.
claims.reason: Current citations proxy popularity rather than historical popularity; metadata may be missing.

claims.claim: Large-team work attracts earlier attention; small-team and disruptive work receive delayed recognition.
claims.evidence_needed: Annual attention profiles on comparable complete follow-up, by team size and disruption, with uncertainty.
claims.reason: Only early timing; no long-term sleeping-beauty assessment.

claims.claim: Team-size association mostly remains with year, topic and author fixed effects and across paper designs/types.
claims.evidence_needed: Comparable-sample fixed-effect gradients and review/non-review contrasts where labelled.
claims.reason: Limited within-author support; theory/empirical labels not established; not causal.

claims.claim: Team-size association persists across citation windows and disruption variants.
claims.evidence_needed: Fixed two-year-window versus main on a common sample, and simplified ratio; assess other variants only if input/budget permits.
claims.reason: No historical 5–40-year follow-up; variants may need additional graph data.

claims.claim: Historical team-size growth, funding/company comparisons, and Nobel disruptiveness provide context.
claims.evidence_needed: Descriptive gradient by recorded funding acknowledgment; no extrapolation to historical, company-patent or Nobel comparisons.
claims.reason: Local funder data exist; historical corpus, requisite company patents and prize labels absent.
